reason: Section 4 contains separate topics: corporate existence and general municipal powers, internal municipal organization and delegation, and recovery after a person defaults on a council direction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal perpetual succession and general corporate powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(1) and 4(2) state perpetual succession and list general corporate powers to sue, contract, charge interest, hold property and take security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s perpetual succession and general corporate powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal committees, departments and delegated administrative powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 4(3) separately authorizes municipal internal bodies and delegation of administrative powers and duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s power to create or alter internal bodies and delegate administrative powers and duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal action to recover expense and damages after default
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 4(4) separately allows council to cause a defaulted thing to be done and recover expense, costs and damages.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what council may recover when a person defaults on something lawfully ordered or directed by council.

reason: Section 5 is a coherent document-execution rule requiring a corporate seal and, except as provided by regulation, sealing and mayor-clerk signatures for municipal documents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal corporate seal and document signing requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the municipal seal and the sealing and signing requirements for agreements, contracts, deeds and other documents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the corporate seal and signing requirements for municipal documents.

reason: Section 6 is one application rule excluding municipalities and rural communities from the Corporations Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporations Act non-application to municipalities and rural communities

evidenceText: does not apply to a municipality or a rural community

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains a single non-application rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Corporations Act does not apply to a municipality or rural community.

reason: Section 6.1 is one nuisance-immunity rule for specified water overflow and wastewater or storm-water systems, with a temporal exception for earlier causes of action.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal nuisance immunity for overflow and wastewater or storm-water systems
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the scope of nuisance immunity and its non-application to causes of action arising before commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a municipality is immune from nuisance liability for overflow or wastewater and storm-water systems and when that immunity does not apply.

reason: Section 7 separates municipal service authority and mandatory police protection from the powers to acquire land, enter service agreements and participate in natural gas or airport arrangements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal service authority, police protection and service administration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7(1) to 7(3) state which services may or must be provided and who administers, pays for and may make by-laws about them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall municipal service authority, the police protection duty, and how service powers are administered and funded.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land acquisition and agreements for municipal services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 7(4) separately authorizes acquiring adjacent land and entering agreements for shared costs, joint service arrangements and sewerage or water works.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the land acquisition and agreement powers a municipality may use when providing services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Natural gas distribution and airport commission agreements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7(5) and 7(6) separately address agreements respecting natural gas distribution systems and airport commission participation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s powers to enter natural gas distribution and airport commission agreements.

reason: Section 7.1 is too broad for one unit because it covers garbage by-law content, user-charge recovery and accounting, payment and debt collection, compelled service use, and rural community application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Garbage and refuse by-law content
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 7.1(1) lists what a garbage and refuse collection and disposal by-law may prescribe, prohibit or restrict.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a municipal garbage and refuse collection and disposal by-law may regulate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Garbage user-charge recovery, accounting, meaning and payment terms
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7.1(2) to 7.1(5) and 7.1(8) address user-charge cost recovery, dedicated use of money, surplus or deficit treatment, the meaning of user-charge, payment terms and debt recovery.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how garbage service user-charges may be established, used, defined, paid and recovered.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compelled use of garbage service and charge if not used
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7.1(6) and 7.1(7) address compelling owners to use the service or charging them if the service is not used, with assessment near the user-charge.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a municipality may compel use of garbage service or charge an owner who does not use it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Garbage by-law definitions and rural community application
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7.1(9) and 7.1(10) address by-law definitions for garbage purposes and application to rural communities with necessary modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the garbage by-law definition power and how the section applies to rural communities.

reason: Section 8 is a focused expropriation power with a clear boundary: municipalities may expropriate for services or powers, but not within another municipality or rural community.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal expropriation power and invalid cross-boundary expropriation
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections define the expropriation power and prohibit expropriation within another municipality or rural community.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a municipality may expropriate and when a purported expropriation is invalid.

reason: Section 9 is one council-authority rule vesting municipal powers in council and allowing a new council to continue proceedings begun by a previous council.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Council exercise of municipal powers and continuation of proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address council as the body exercising municipal powers and the continuity of proceedings between councils.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who exercises municipal powers and how a new council may continue previous council proceedings.

reason: Section 10 is a focused council-meetings rule setting the first-meeting timing after election and the minimum number of regular meetings each year.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council meeting timing and annual regular meetings
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address the clerk-fixed first meeting, the default fourth Monday of May meeting and the four-regular-meetings annual minimum.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the first council meeting is held after election and how many regular meetings council must hold each year.

reason: Section 10.1 is one open-voting rule, with an exception allowing the mayor to vote only as a casting vote where authorized by procedural by-law, charter or special Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Open individual council voting and mayor casting-vote exception
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address open individual voting, no secret ballot, recording votes and the possible mayor casting-vote exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council votes must be announced and recorded and when the mayor may be limited to a casting vote.

reason: Section 10.2 separates open-meeting and decision-validity rules from closed-meeting grounds and the limits and records that apply after a meeting is closed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Open council and committee meetings and valid council decisions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.2(1) to 10.2(3) require regular and special council meetings and committee meetings to be public and require council decisions to be made and authorized by by-law or resolution at a meeting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the open-meeting rules and what makes a council act or decision valid.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Grounds for excluding the public from council or committee discussions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 10.2(4) lists the matters that may justify excluding the public from a meeting for the duration of the discussion.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the categories of matters that may be discussed in a closed council or committee meeting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Closed committee decision limits and public record of closed meetings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10.2(5) to 10.2(7) restrict decisions at closed committee meetings and require a limited record available to the public.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what decisions may be made in a closed committee meeting and what public record must be kept.

reason: Section 10.3 is a single procedural by-law duty with an exception where prescribed matters conflict with a charter or private or special Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mandatory procedural by-law and charter conflict exception
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the duty to enact a council meeting procedural by-law and the exception for conflicts with a municipal charter or private or special Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a municipal procedural by-law must cover and when prescribed matters may be omitted.

reason: Section 11 combines a broad set of municipal by-law powers with a separate special-meeting rule limiting business to the notice unless unanimous consent is given.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal by-law powers for fees, licensing, retail operation, devices, signs, noise and tax collection

evidenceText: noise likely to cause a public nuisance

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 11(1) lists by-law powers over recreational fees, taxi licensing, retail business on weekly day of rest, transient traders, guns and air rifles, exhibitions, amusement places, signs, vending machines, noise and tax collection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main by-law powers listed in section 11 for municipal fees, licensing, retail operations, signs, devices, noise and tax collection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special meeting business limited to notice unless unanimous consent
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 11(2) separately restricts special-meeting business to what is specified in the notice unless all members present unanimously consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what business council may consider at a special meeting.

reason: Section 11.1 is one alternative-notice rule allowing radio, television or municipal website notice instead of newspaper publication if the notice is also available at the clerk’s office.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Alternative municipal notice by broadcast or website with clerk-office availability
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address authorized alternatives to newspaper notice and the clerk-office availability condition for sufficiency.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a municipality may give alternative notice by broadcast or website and what extra availability condition applies.
